docs.title: Teaching feedback scaffolding
docs.text:
• Observable behavior: (Describe an action the learner can demonstrate, its LO and verification evidence.)
  • Failed version of the same task: (Retain the input, generated result and evidence of failed verification.)
  • Diagnosis: (Use evidence to locate an assumption or implementation problem, rather than only copying an error message.)
  • Improved version: (Record revision differences; re-verify the same input and boundary inputs.)
  • Timebox and checkpoints: (Expected minutes; inspect artifacts at the checkpoint; when stuck, record the current state and ask for help.)
  • Hint ladder: (Begin with a question that locates the problem, then a related concept, then partial steps; record the level actually used.)
  • Formative feedback: (At least once; feedback source, time, evidence and actionable advice, to be completed.)
  • Visible revision: (At least once; before/after differences and re-verification results, to be completed; reuse the current file or existing activities.)
  • Teaching/rehearsal evidence: (Awaiting human completion; record pseudonymous roles, environment, timing, accessibility issues, failures and references to repair evidence.)

These fields serve teaching feedback only. They do not add weekly required files or change the eight-dimension rubric or grading contract. The template's existence, complete fields or passing automated checks do not mean that human teaching/rehearsal, calibration or approval has taken place.

docs.title: AI-use note
docs.text:
Complete this once in the existing description for each assignment or milestone. PRs reference the same evidence ID. There is no separate submission of this file or repeated signature requirement.

  • Assignment or milestone and evidence ID:
  • AI use: none; or the tool/model, purpose and verification I personally completed.
  • Artifact, verification results and brief explanation: reference existing paths without copying the content.

Only when this assignment or milestone explicitly requires trajectories, include the required redacted excerpts or their paths; do not export the entire chat. Remove keys, unrelated personal information and unauthorized data. If required evidence encounters a technical failure, describe the impact and available alternative evidence in the same note and follow the course's supplementary-evidence process. Assignments that do not require logs do not enter that process merely because logs are absent.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Use this design document for the week 4 specification. It turns the proposal into a testable boundary and records decisions that another reader can challenge.

docs.title: Requirements and acceptance cases
docs.text:
For each requirement, give normal, boundary and failure cases with observable outcomes.

ID Requirement Normal case and outcome Boundary case and outcome Failure case and outcome R-__

docs.text:
For every decision, record the choice, evidence, and one alternative you rejected. Say what new evidence would make you revisit it.

Decision Chosen approach Rejected alternative and reason Revisit evidence D-__

docs.title: Interfaces and data models
docs.text: Describe inputs, outputs, errors, side effects and permissions for each public interface. Show the data entities, required fields, relationships and invariants. Include a small example for the core scenario; use synthetic values.

docs.title: Test strategy
docs.text: Name the unit, integration and end-to-end checks, their fixtures, and the property or invariant each check protects. State how you will run mutation testing and investigate surviving mutants. Identify the regression that should fail on the starting revision.

docs.title: Agent workflow and gates
docs.text: List the repository instruction file, hook gate, permitted tools and verification command. Explain what the gate blocks and how you will test both a blocked and an allowed change.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: List features, integrations, data and failure modes you will not build for this milestone. Explain how each exclusion protects the core scenario or keeps verification possible.

docs.title: AI-use note
docs.text: State the tool and purpose, or state that no AI was used. Reuse the proposal's note ID when it still describes this work.

docs.title: Review
docs.text: Check that every requirement has an observable outcome, each decision has a rejected alternative, interfaces agree with the data model, and the test strategy can detect a regression. Record the submitted revision and the decision: accept, narrow, re-check or stop, with evidence links.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Complete this reflection without AI assistance. Identify the related assignment or milestone or project and learning outcomes (LOs).

docs.title: Records
docs.text: Original prediction, actual performance, failure evidence and causes of error; how to verify improvement next time. Briefly describe one prediction error, one verification step and the next improvement, without a word-count threshold. Refer to existing assignment evidence by ID rather than copying it again.

docs.title: Review
docs.text: Check the evidence yourself. If you receive feedback, record revisions and re-verification in this same note; do not submit a separate set of feedback forms.

docs.title: Goal and scope
docs.text: Users, problem, non-goals and learning outcomes (LOs).

docs.title: Interview traceability
docs.text: Interview ID / approved equivalent-material ID -> requirement ID -> acceptance criteria ID -> test ID. Do not include real names.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text: Given input, action, expected result, boundaries and failure paths. Each criterion must support executable verification.

docs.title: Implementation and verification
docs.text:
Generate an approach -> have a human check its assumptions -> implement in the dedicated workspace described by Week 0 safety practices -> retain acceptance and regression evidence.

Before implementation, add two scope tables and one location note to the plan:

  1. Changed files: list every file with its relevant path:line (or new for a new file). Only the files in this table may be changed; update the table and obtain another scope check before adding a file.
  2. Tests to write: list each test separately and map it to exactly one acceptance case and its expected result. Every acceptance case must have a named test; a generic “run the suite” entry is not a substitute.
  3. Specification location and update: record where this specification, its plan and decision record live, and how a code change keeps those records and acceptance tests synchronized for the next session.

docs.title: Risks and review
docs.text: Data minimization, permission boundaries, unresolved questions and review results. Refer to existing PR or review evidence; do not submit a separate teaching-design form.

docs.title: Change log
docs.text: One entry per agreed change to an acceptance criterion: the date, the changed clause, the acceptance-case and test IDs it affects, the reason and who agreed. Update those tests' expected results from the new clause first, then the code; never edit a check only to make existing code pass.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Keep the evidence needed to explain one work product. Reuse it by ID across permitted assessments.

docs.title: Artifact and decision
docs.text: Task or milestone ID, revision and the bounded change. State the user need or contract, and whether you accept, narrow, recheck or stop.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: One discriminating input with its independent expected result; the actual command/result or an explicit missing observation. Link any reused test, trace, review or participant record by ID. Keep sensitive records in the approved private location.

docs.title: My explanation and revision
docs.text: Explain why the observation supports the decision. Keep the initial prediction and one change made after feedback. Answer the changed-input question yourself. Use a few sentences; no word-count quota or full chat export.

docs.title: AI-use note
docs.text: Assistance ID; tool/model and purpose, or no AI used. Reuse this ID when the same work feeds another milestone.

docs.title: Review
docs.text: After feedback, record the one change you made and the check that supports it.
